questions.question: US-05.3 and US-06.1 say every employee subject to source tax must answer the denomination and children questions, and Liechtenstein residents count as subject. But the AC-05.7.3 examples show '–' for denomination, children and spouse employment when a Liechtenstein resident returns home daily or has at most 45 non-return days. In that case the result is 'in principle no source tax liability' and needs no tariff inputs. Should Liechtenstein residents with that outcome skip the tariff questions? If so, the Liechtenstein cross-border questions have to come before denomination, spouse employment and children in the flow. Today all of these sit together in step 6.

What is recorded as 'Subject to source tax' for a Liechtenstein resident who gets 'in principle no source tax liability'? Is it 'yes' (lives abroad), 'no', or a third status? Does the recorded liability differ from what the US-05.7 result table shows?

Many new employees move around their start date. Should they enter their current home address, or the address that will apply from the first working day? Someone moving from Germany to Zurich would get a different liability, canton, cross-border questions and tariff depending on the answer. And what about weekly residents who keep a Swiss address but have their main residence abroad?

Does the employee see any of the derived results before or after submitting? These are the insurance start date, whether they are subject to source tax, and the tariff code or Liechtenstein result. The spec only says results are 'recorded for HR'. Showing them (or not) changes the closing and summary screens.

Does the employee type in a blank first working day, or does HR give a pre-filled date (e.g. from the contract) that the employee confirms or corrects? 'Enter and confirm' can be read either way. A pre-filled date needs HR input before the questionnaire starts.
Which first working days are valid? Can the date be in the past, or lie very far in the future? Must it be a weekday? The spec only requires a date.

The evidence for the H tariff (F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b) says a child counts with H only when it lives in the employee's household. Row 22 of the child result table, which is not marked inferred, gives 'counts with H' for a minor child outside the household (single parent with custody, alternating care, employee pays more). Which is correct? The answer changes A vs H in the tariff code.

On what date is a child's status (minor, or of age and in first education) judged: the day the questionnaire is filled in, the first working day, or the start of the tax year? This matters for a child who turns 18 around the start date.

For married employees and registered partners the children question includes the spouse's children. For such a stepchild, the custody, 'other parent' and maintenance questions are worded for the employee's own child. Should the wording change for stepchildren, or should those questions be answered from the spouse's point of view?

'HR words the reminder': is this a fixed text HR gives us once, or must HR be able to edit it themselves (per customer company, over time)? HR editing it would need a content setting that does not exist in the employee-side scope.

D-036 says inapplicable answers 'may be kept' until submission, but AC-08.2.1 requires them to come back when the earlier answer is switched back. Is keeping them mandatory? Should progress also survive closing the questionnaire and coming back later (save and resume)? Nothing is said about a partly completed questionnaire across sessions.
Every address part is required, but some valid postal addresses have no house number, such as rural addresses or named buildings. Should the questionnaire accept an address without a house number?

The AC-01.2.1 example table gives '–' for the country of a Swiss resident but 'required' for a German resident, although the text says country is always required. AC-01.3.2 mixes '–' and 'not asked' for the canton in the same way. Do '–' and 'not asked' mean the same thing in these tables, so the examples can be used as test cases?
Should first and last name be the official names as on the ID document, including all first names? Or is the name the employee normally uses enough for the pension fund registration?

tech_leaks.quote: the employee is asked for their first working day at Muster AG as a date (DD.MM.YYYY)
tech_leaks.why: The DD.MM.YYYY format comes from the fund's date-of-birth and insurance-start-date fields and from G-10, which sets the wording used in the spec's examples. No stakeholder asks for the first working day to be typed in this format. How the date is entered is a UI decision.

tech_leaks.quote: the employee can add further children and remove a child, and the child questions repeat per child
tech_leaks.why: This copies the calculator's add/remove child buttons as an interaction pattern. The business need is only that every child can be described. How several children are entered is a UI decision.

The Notes rows fix a step number for each question (step 1 personal, 2 address, 3 employment, 4 residence status, 5 family, 6 source tax). This is screen sequencing beyond the business dependencies, and it limits the reordering that conditional skipping needs, for example for Liechtenstein.
